one_liner: Online payment processing platform for accepting payments, subscriptions, invoicing, and broader financial infrastructure (Connect, Treasury, Issuing).
access_note: Test-mode API keys are available instantly on signup and fully functional for building; live/production keys require completing business verification (KYB) before real money can move.
api_breadth_note: Covers payments, subscriptions/billing, invoicing, Connect marketplaces, Treasury, Tax, Radar fraud detection, card Issuing, and more.
existing_mcp_note: Official Stripe MCP server (also the stripe-agent-toolkit), offering account reads, writes, and doc search.

evidence.note: Confirms API key-based Basic Auth model, test vs live key prefixes.

researcher_notes: Very well documented; the only nuance is that live-mode charges require KYB, standard for fintech.

one_liner: Financial data connectivity API that links apps to users' bank accounts for balances, transactions, identity, auth, and more.
access_note: Sandbox environment (fake institutions/data) is free and instantly self-serve after signup; Production access requires submitting a 'Migrate to Production' application and passing Plaid's review.
api_breadth_note: Auth, Transactions, Identity, Balance, Investments, Liabilities, Income, Transfer, and more across many financial institutions.
existing_mcp_note: Plaid publishes an official Dashboard MCP server and an official local AI coding toolkit MCP server for development.

evidence.note: API overview confirming client_id/secret API-key auth model.
Confirms free self-serve Sandbox and separate Production approval process.

researcher_notes: Production requires real bank-linking approval and billing setup, typical for account-aggregation fintechs.

one_liner: Cryptocurrency exchange offering spot/margin/futures trading, market data, wallet, and staking APIs.
access_note: Testnet/Demo Trading API keys are free and self-serve; live trading keys require a verified, KYC'd Binance account and are subject to regional regulatory restrictions.
api_breadth_note: Spot, margin, futures, wallet, staking, NFT, Pay, sub-accounts, and FIX/WebSocket variants.
existing_mcp_note: Multiple unofficial community MCP servers exist; no official Binance-published MCP server found.
main_blocker: Live trading requires KYC-verified account and is geographically restricted in some jurisdictions.

evidence.note: Confirms free self-serve testnet keys and HMAC/RSA/Ed25519 auth.

one_liner: A payment-gateway product name that could not be independently verified; the hint suggests an NMI-powered white-label gateway, but no dedicated public developer docs for 'Paygent Connect' were found.
access_note: No standalone 'Paygent Connect' developer portal exists; if genuinely an NMI white-label reseller product, it would inherit NMI's model of self-serve sandbox exploration plus a gated merchant/reseller underwriting application for production.
api_breadth_note: Could not locate an actual endpoint list or reference specific to 'Paygent Connect'.
existing_mcp_note: No MCP server found under the name 'Paygent Connect'. NMI itself has a documentation-only MCP server that provides no account/transaction access.
main_blocker: Could not locate a public developer portal or API reference specifically for 'Paygent Connect'; the name 'Paygent' is heavily overloaded across several unrelated companies.

evidence.note: NMI's own API (the presumed underlying gateway) uses API-key auth, self-serve sandbox, and gated merchant sign-up.
Shows a distinct, unrelated 'Paygent' (Japanese bank-transfer processor).

researcher_notes: Needs human verification — despite extensive searching, no company or product called exactly 'Paygent Connect' powered by NMI could be confirmed.

one_liner: iPayX Protocol is a FINTRAC-registered FX forensic audit tool that compares bank/card FX rates against live mid-market rates to expose hidden currency-conversion fees — not a payment processor despite the name.
access_note: Three of four MCP tools (rate lookup, transaction audit, multi-source comparison) work with zero signup or API key; only the 'full forensic report' tool requires a free API key.
api_breadth_note: Only four tools, all focused on FX-rate auditing/comparison — a single-purpose utility, not a broad financial API.
existing_mcp_note: The product itself ships as an MCP server, published by the company's own GitHub org and linked directly from ipayx.ai — this MCP server effectively is the public API.

evidence.note: Official README documenting all 4 tools, auth requirements, and installation.
Confirms company identity as a FINTRAC-registered FX audit layer, not a payment processor.

researcher_notes: Surprising find: no conventional REST API reference page — the actual integration surface is the MCP server itself.

one_liner: Intuit's cloud accounting platform; the QuickBooks Online API lets apps read/write invoices, customers, payments, and other accounting data.
access_note: Free developer account, OAuth2 app registration, and a sandbox company file are self-serve on developer.intuit.com; serving real customers in production requires passing Intuit's app review/compliance process.
api_breadth_note: Full accounting object model (invoices, bills, customers, vendors, payments, reports) plus separate Payments and Payroll APIs.
existing_mcp_note: No official Intuit-published MCP server found; community packages exist.
main_blocker: Production/app-store approval is needed to serve real, non-developer customers at scale (sandbox alone is fine for a demo).

evidence.note: Developer portal entry point (JS SPA, could not render past loading screen).

researcher_notes: developer.intuit.com is a heavy JS SPA that resisted automated fetching — recommend a human browser check to confirm current details.

one_liner: Cloud accounting software; the Xero API exposes accounting, payroll, and practice-management data (invoices, contacts, bank transactions, etc.).
access_note: Free developer account and OAuth2 app registration are self-serve, with a demo company for testing; apps can connect to up to 25 real organizations without any review.
api_breadth_note: Accounting API, Payroll APIs (multiple regions), Assets, Projects, Files, and Practice Manager.
existing_mcp_note: Official Xero MCP server published as @xeroapi/xero-mcp-server on npm, maintained by Xero staff.

evidence.note: Confirms OAuth2 as the API auth model (JS-rendered page, metadata confirmed).
npm registry confirms an official Xero-maintained MCP package.

researcher_notes: developer.xero.com is a JS-rendered site that resisted full fetching — details cross-checked against confirmed page titles and the verified official MCP npm package.

one_liner: Corporate card and spend-management platform; Brex APIs manage cards, expenses, bills, accounting sync, and payments.
access_note: Brex's own quickstart guide states it 'assumes you are a Brex customer with admin access to your dashboard' — there is no public sandbox for outside developers.
api_breadth_note: Accounting, Budgets, Expenses, Fields, Onboarding, Payments, Team, Transactions, Travel, and Webhooks APIs.
existing_mcp_note: Official Brex MCP server, supporting both OAuth (recommended) and API-key Bearer auth, with ~35 tools.
main_blocker: Requires an existing, funded Brex business account with admin access to obtain any credentials.

evidence.note: API overview listing all REST APIs.
Explicitly states the API requires an existing Brex customer account with admin access.

researcher_notes: Notably transparent and detailed official MCP docs, including a full tools table.

one_liner: Corporate card and spend-management platform; the Ramp API manages cards, transactions, bills, vendor payouts, and accounting sync.
access_note: Ramp's Technology Partner program grants free 'Sandbox and Developer Console access' to anyone who signs up at the entry Partner tier, but production access to real spend data requires being an approved Ramp customer or partner.
api_breadth_note: Cards, transactions/receipts/reimbursements, bills/AP, vendor payouts, spend controls & provisioning, embedded virtual cards, accounting sync.
existing_mcp_note: Ramp's partner marketing page lists 'MCP connectors' as a first-party capability; exact server URL/tool list could not be confirmed since docs.ramp.com is a JS-only SPA.
main_blocker: Production API access requires partner or customer approval; primary docs site could not be fully rendered to verify exact details.

evidence.note: Confirms free Sandbox/Developer Console access at entry tier and lists MCP connectors.
Official API documentation site (JS-rendered, not directly readable).

researcher_notes: Ramp explicitly advertises MCP support, but the docs.ramp.com SPA blocked direct verification — should be spot-checked in a browser.

one_liner: Private capital markets data platform (companies, deals, investors, funds) for market intelligence, deal sourcing, and due diligence.
access_note: There is no public self-serve signup or API key; the 'Direct Data' page is purely a lead-generation form — access requires a sales conversation and a commercial contract.
api_breadth_note: No public API reference is available; marketing copy only mentions on-demand calls and scheduled feeds covering companies, deals, investors, and funds.
existing_mcp_note: No official or community MCP server found.
main_blocker: No public developer docs, API reference, or self-serve credentials exist; access requires a sales conversation and commercial contract with undisclosed terms/pricing.

evidence.note: Confirms API/Data Feed access is a lead-gen contact-sales form, not self-serve.
Confirms overall product is a subscription research/data platform.

researcher_notes: Confirms the assignment's own hint — PitchBook is a licensed data product with no self-serve public API.
